text:
alisa: ran a quick nsys on nightly master with the 8xA100 perf harness, seeing a new hotspot sweep. attaching the top kernel breakdown I pulled from the trace.

mike: thanks — can you paste the top kernel list?

alisa: sure, pasted below (total GPU active time = 89.2s):
- softmax_forward_f32                32.6s   (36.5%)
- matmul_128x128_tma                 19.7s   (22.1%)
- attention_kv_reorder               8.7s    (9.8%)
- kv_cache_lookup                    6.5s    (7.3%)
- layernorm_fused                    5.9s    (6.6%)
- continuous_batch_dispatch          3.4s    (3.8%)
- dropout_trinary                    2.5s    (2.8%)
- other kernels                      10.9s   (12.2%)

alisa: notable: softmax is huge now vs last week's baseline where matmul dominated. heatmap shows softmax kernels firing a lot on short seqs and small heads.

jordan: interesting — did kernel selector change recently? last PR for kernel selection tweaked heuristics for head_dim=64 to favor faster numerics. @devon any recent selector changes?

devon: I merged a fallback chain change two days ago that added a vectorized softmax variant when seq_len <= 128 and head_dim%32==0. It was meant to save memory but might be slower on high throughput.

mike: can you paste the nsys event timeline snippet for softmax? warp efficiency / SM occupancy numbers?

alisa: timeline snippet: 
softmax_forward_f32: avg duration 48.2us, calls 676k, avg SM util 85%, avg occupancy 21%.
matmul_128x128_tma: avg duration 210us, calls 94k, avg SM util 98%, avg occupancy 42%.
kv_cache_lookup: spikes at seq_break boundaries, lots of small kernels (~5-12us) causing scheduling pressure.

jordan: occupancy low on softmax but sm util high — suggests few active warps but they saturate memory? or reduction across threads causing serialization. Could be the new vectorized softmax using atomics or a loop-stride pattern.

devon: the fallback introduced an extra transposition step before softmax for certain layouts. That transposition runs as separate kernels (we see attention_kv_reorder). Combined cost might make softmax > matmul for short sequences.

perf-bot: nightly-regressions: detected +18% GPU time on generation workload vs 2026-03-10 baseline. Top contributors: softmax_forward_f32 (+29%), attention_kv_reorder (+14%). Ticket auto-filed: PERF-4721.

alisa: ok action items I propose:
1) revert vectorized-softmax fallback on nightly and rerun nsys to verify regression scope.
2) add micro-bench for softmax variants (seq_len in [32,64,128,256], head_dim [32,64,128]) to compare throughput.
3) instrument kernel selector to emit chosen_variant metadata (so we can map trace kernels -> selector decision).
4) evaluate merging transposition into combined kernel to avoid separate reorder kernel.

mike: +1. also try increasing batching window in harness to see if batching hides the regression (we might be paying cost only in many small micro-batches).

jordan: I'll take 2 and 3. can you assign PERF-4721 to me and link the microbench results there?

devon: I'll open a small revert PR for the fallback and run a perf job. expect results in ~1.5h.

perf-bot: job run queued: perf/job/29321-vecsoftmax-revert. estimated completion 90m.

alisa: great. one extra note: KV cache lookup shows many tiny kernels at sequence boundaries that create high kernel-launch overhead. if we can coalesce those lookups into a single batched kernel for small batches it would reduce overhead.

mike: agree — maybe a tiny TTL-based cache aggregation layer in dispatcher. low risk experiment.

jordan: logging plan: I'll attach microbench csvs and annotated nsys (.qdrep) urls into the ticket. keep any full traces but trim PII.

devon: PR up: revert diff (link). starting perf run now.

alisa: thanks team — please update PERF-4721 with findings. I'll monitor console alerts in case error budgets spike. :thumbsup:
